text: The Delhi sultans faced the enemy the rest of Asia feared most, the Mongols.
China, Persia, and Russia all fell to them.
One sultan threw back invasion after invasion.
He also fixed the prices of grain, horses, and cloth in the markets of Delhi
one of history's first price regulators, a very, very strict one.
But the sultan everyone remembers came a little later,
Clever, well-read, full of big ideas,
and with possibly the worst timing of any ruler in Indian history.
In 1327, he decided his capital was in the wrong place, so he moved it from Delhi to
Dalatabad, about a thousand kilometers south.
And he didn't just move the court, he ordered much of Delhi's population to move with him.
